parameters.content:
## ATTACH, DON'T DUPLICATE

One handler serves EVERY parent workflow: set
**Settings -> Error workflow** on each parent to this workflow.
(The composed workflows ship with
`settings.errorWorkflow = "REPLACE_WITH_WF_ERROR_HANDLER_ID"` -
swap in this workflow's real ID after import.)

This workflow does **not** need to be activated to work.

Payload gotcha: if a parent's own TRIGGER fails, there is no
`execution` object at all - the payload is `trigger{}` instead.
The Code node branches on that; do not "simplify" it away.

nodes.name: STICKY - How to attach this handler

parameters.content:
## NOTIFY = GENERIC WEBHOOK PLACEHOLDER

template-1326's skeleton is `Error Trigger -> Slack`. **Slack was
deliberately swapped out**: the owner has not picked a channel.

Current: HTTP Request POST to `{{ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL}}` with
`onError: continueRegularOutput` so a bad/unset URL can never turn
the error handler itself into a second failure. It then falls
through to a No-Op sink, so failures are always visible in the
execution list even with no channel wired.

**OWNER DECISION NEEDED:** Slack / ntfy / email / platform inbox /
Temporal-side alerting. Swap the one node, keep everything else.

nodes.name: STICKY - Notification channel is an OWNER CHOICE

parameters.content:
## PLACEHOLDERS
- `{{ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL}}` - notification endpoint (owner's choice)
- Credential **ALERT_WEBHOOK_AUTH (placeholder)** - generic
  `httpHeaderAuth`; DELETE the auth block entirely if the chosen
  channel needs none.

## CANNIBALIZED FROM
- **template-1326** "Get a Slack alert when a workflow went wrong"
  (n8n.io/workflows/1326) - the entire 2-node skeleton
  `errorTrigger -> notify`, kept as-is; only the notify node was
  swapped. Its `alwaysOutputData: true` on the trigger is kept.
- **native docs** Error Trigger payload shape (both variants).
